regions.why: Left tip-vortex corridor is only 0.18% covered and its declared span (0.04981 m) is the tightest of the three; level 3 gives 0.03125 m, a factor 1.6 below the requirement, and overlaps the wake box so the union is one equal-level block along the vortex path (no transition defect inside the corridor).

regions.why: Mirror tip-vortex corridor with identical 0.04981 m span requirement; level 3 = 0.03125 m meets it. advisor.hypothesis: The mesh is a first attempt with no native failure evidence; the one measured, deterministic defect is that the off-body requirements are effectively unrefined (configured coverage 0.00386 / 0.00182 / 0.00181). Cause: refinement is purely distance-driven around the body (bands 0.03125 m @ L4 and 0.09375 m @ L3) plus one level-6 near-trailing-edge feature box; nothing follows the flow downstream of X=0.996. The trailing-edge vorticity sheet and the two tip-vortex corridors are transport features, not proximity features, so they must be prescribed explicitly. Fixing this with three flow_refine boxes at level 3 (0.25/2^3 = 0.03125 m) satisfies both declared spans with margin (wake 0.03125 < 0.06226 m; tips 0.03125 < 0.04981 m), keeps the level jump to the level-4 surface mesh at exactly one level (n_cells_between_levels=3 inserts a buffer), and is consistent with the existing level-3 outer distance band so the union is a single level-3 block with no internal transition. Level 3 is the coarsest level that meets the strict max axis span; level 2 (0.0625 m) would exceed the tip span (0.0625 > 0.0498) and would only pass via the native p95 1.5x tolerance, and level 4 would cost ~680k extra cells and break the 2M gate. I deliberately do NOT touch layers, first height, n_grow or snap: there is no native extrusion/quality evidence yet, and the planning y+ estimate (h1 = 1.1087e-3 m, y+~50, stack 0.01829 m) is a surrogate, not a measurement.
advisor.expected_change: Scenario screen flips from accepted=false to accepted=true with configured volume coverage 0.00386/0.00182/0.00181 -> 1.0/1.0/1.0 for lift_wake/tip_left/tip_right, and nominal corridor cell size becomes 0.03125 m everywhere inside the corridors instead of 0.25 m background and 0.0625 m in the un-banded wake, downstream to X=2.9886 (3 chords past the trailing edge). Conservative cell forecast rises 1,693,778 -> 1,821,185 (91% of the 2,000,000 budget, +85k, i.e. less than the naive 8x-per-increment because the union of the three equal-level boxes is refined once). Uncertainty: the forecast is an unvalidated geometry upper bound and actual native cell count is a hard gate; the corridors themselves remain unvalidated hypotheses, so this intervention fixes resolution allocation, not vortex position or flow accuracy.
counterevidence: The corridors are unvalidated_physical_hypothesis: incidence/deflection may move the rolled-up tip vortex, so refining exactly the declared envelope could still miss the physical core - I keep the boxes matched to the requirement bounds instead of spending the remaining 9% budget on speculative enlargement.

Geometry measurements show p5 solid_normal_half_thickness 0.00845 m at thin TE/tip stations versus a requested layer stack of 0.01829 m and max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3, and 33.4% of adjacent edges exceed the 60 deg layer feature angle, so extrusion may still trim or drop layers at the TE/tip - that is a separate mechanism with no native evidence yet.

unresolved_feature_fraction stays 0.0366 with and without the new boxes, confirming that off-body refinement does not address the unresolved sub-grid cluster and must not be sold as a geometry-fidelity fix.
Steady RANS mesh allocation cannot validate wake recovery or any unsteady shedding implied by the vorticity-sheet mechanism.
alternatives: Refine the same three corridors at level 4 (0.015625 m): passes spans with large margin but adds ~680k cells (conservative total ~2.37M) and would exceed max_global_cells, so it is not admissible now.
Refine the wake at level 2 (0.0625 m) to save ~43k cells: rejected because 0.0625 m exceeds the declared tip max span 0.04981 m and only the native p95 1.5x tolerance would mask it for the wake.

Widen refinement_bands (e.g. inner 0.03125 m @ L4, outer 0.15 m @ L3) to give the medial-axis shrinker more room around the thin TE/tip: deferred - it is cheap but unevidenced, and the thin-station half-thickness above suggests the shrinker, not the band depth, is the controlling risk.
Enlarge/shift the corridors beyond their declared bounds to hedge vortex drift: deferred until a flow solution exists, since it consumes the remaining budget margin with no measured trajectory.

Whole-body extraction is 69.27% and global layer coverage is 0.674. The second mechanism is the shrinker: displacementMedialAxis is the mesh-motion solver that refuses to shrink the normal spacing, so the last 2–3 layer nodes are compressed to near-zero-height cells and inverted; the cluster sits 0.0256 m from the wall, i.e. at the outer layer rows. Two coupled layer-construction defects are the real mechanism. (1) The medial-axis shrinker reports "Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes" and "Written 0 points ..." in both outer passes, yet extrudes only 68.5% of wall faces (51482/75141, identical in pass 1 and 2: 52041->52033 faces). Truncation is therefore all-or-nothing DISABLED EXTRUSION, not thickness compression; those faces keep the full 8-layer stack definition at collapsed height, which is exactly the pattern in the data: only counts 0-4 are inflated (9.8/6.8/6.4/5.3/4.3%) while counts 5,6,7 are uniform at ~4.1% each and 8 holds 54.6%. Non-extruded/downgraded columns adjacent to full-height 8-layer columns shear into zero/negative volume, high aspect (2.8e95), wrong-oriented faces and skew 84. (2) The dominant cause of the 68.5% loss is the corner/crease geometry: 33.4% of body edges exceed feature_angle=60 and the dihedral p95 is 90 deg (sharp TE and tip corners). At feature_angle=60 those 90 deg creases receive corner extrusion, whose columns collide, and the medial-axis mover cannot recover. I deliberately do NOT add flow_refine boxes: cells are 1.234M of a 2M gate and the corridors already pass; I only delete the round-1 fallback repair_0 level-5 box, which inserted an unrequested level-5/level-4 step inside the existing band and sits on the layer-collapse site.
advisor.expected_change: Layer coverage 0.674 -> target >0.90 with n_surface_layers=5; nonpositive cells 159 -> 0 and max_aspect 2.8e95 -> <1000, because the collapsed-column/wrong-oriented cohort is inside the disabled-extrusion region whose height is now consistent at 5 layers. Co-reduction of expansion_ratio to 1.10 keeps y+ p50 ~50 and the stack at ~6.7 mm, so the corner/mid-chord columns have room. Off-body wake/tip native spans, fidelity (p99 8.74e-4 m, volume 9.1e-4) and cell count (~1.23M) are expected to be unchanged since no flow box is added. Uncertainty: the 33.4%-above-60-deg edge fraction is measured on a 4096-sample subset, and the medial-axis mover could still refuse a fraction of the sharp TE/tip creases; if coverage stalls below 0.90 the next distinct mechanism is slip_feature_angle relaxation toward 75-90 with n_smooth_surface_normals raised, not further box addition.

actions.why: Attack the measured all-or-nothing extrusion failure directly: the driver reduced thickness at 0 nodes and wrote 0 truncation points while dropping 31.5% of wall faces, with only counts 0-4 inflated and counts 5-8 a full-height stack sitting on collapsed columns. advisor.hypothesis: Measured geometry rules out under-resolution and over-refinement as the driver: the failing cells sit where solid normal half-thickness is p50 0.0263 m (p5 0.0205) while the requested layer stack is 0.018292 m — 70–89% of the local solid half-thickness, i.e. the extrusion column is geometrically oversized, and the native log confirms it (Extruding 51067/75166 = 67.9% of body faces, identical in both outer passes, 'Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes', 0 truncation lines retained: an all-or-nothing NOEXTRUDE failure, not thickness compression). Non-extruded/downgraded columns adjacent to full 8-layer columns shear into the 236 zero/negative-volume cells, aspect 2.8e95, 1283 misoriented face pyramids and skew 608. Mechanism is therefore total layer thickness vs available wall-normal room, worsened by corner extrusion: 34.3% of adjacent edges exceed feature_angle=60 (dihedral p95 = 90° at the TE/tip creases), so crease columns collide and the medial-axis mover cannot recover them. Fix: reduce installed total thickness by ~22% so the stack fits comfortably under local half-thickness, drop feature_angle to 45 to suppress extrusion at the ~50–90° creases, and raise max_thickness_to_medial_ratio so the medial-distance limiter acts softly before inversion. Keep first height unchanged (0.0011087 m, y+~50 planning surrogate; no sane measured flow, so wall_height is not eligible).

Off-body corridors already pass natively (p95 span 0.0317 m vs 0.0623/0.0498 m tolerances) and are untouched. advisor.hypothesis: The failure is a LAYER-EXTRUSION/TRANSITION defect localised on the trailing-edge strip, not under-resolution. Native log: only 51275/75174 faces (68.2%) extruded, both outer passes identical, \"Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes\", 0 retained truncation lines, 4 isolated points stopped => all-or-nothing NON-EXTRUSION with no thickness compression, so non-extruded columns sit beside full-height 8-layer columns and shear into the 194 zero/negative-volume cells, aspect 2.8e95, 1079 misoriented pyramids and skew 649. Localisation: the TE strip X 0.90-1.05 has solid normal half-thickness p50 = 0.00735 m (p5 0.00084) while the requested stack is 0.01829 m = 2.5x that; and 50.8-54.3% of adjacent edges there are above layer feature_angle=60 with dihedral p50 = p95 = 90 deg. So the TE crease triggers corner/edge-disabled extrusion and the stack cannot fit the local wall-normal room. The X 0.6-0.9 strip is thinner (p50 0.029 m, 54% edges >60 deg, 0-layer fraction 0.198) and is a secondary loss site. Smooth regions (feature_0) already hold 54.4% full 8 layers, so the stack itself is fine where there is room. Counterevidence respected: fluid_gap_metres is null and finite outward-ray fraction is 0.0 everywhere, so rays prove nothing about gaps; I therefore do NOT treat the region as gap-free, but I also do not invent a gap. The medial distance, not the solid half-thickness, is the shrinker's limiting quantity, so I lower max_thickness_to_medial_ratio so the limiter acts (halving toward min_thickness) instead of the column inverting. Also, thickness reduction at 0 nodes proves the limiter never engaged - it was configured too permissively for the real medial distance. Mechanism fix = (a) make the limiter engage softly, (b) suppress extrusion at the 90 deg TE/tip creases by lowering layer feature_angle below 60, (c) trim the stack so 5+ layers survive on >=90% of area. I keep first height 0.001108680899312848 m (y+~50 surrogate; no sane measured flow, so wall_height is not eligible) and do NOT add flow boxes: all three corridors already pass natively (occupancy 1.0, p95 span 0.0317 m vs 0.0623/0.0498 m) at 1.235M of a 2M gate.
advisor.expected_change: Native extrusion fraction 68.2% -> target >90% of 75174 body faces; zero/negative-volume cells 194 -> 0; max_aspect 2.8e95 -> <1000; wrong-oriented face pyramids 1079 -> 0; skew 649 -> <4; non-ortho 179.8 -> <70; body area with >=5 layers 0.669 -> >=0.90; expected cells ~1.20-1.25M (at or below the 1.235M baseline, well under the 2M gate). Uncertainty: if TE creases still disable extrusion, coverage will plateau and the remaining lever is slip_feature_angle/n_buffer_cells_no_extrude, which I have left at baseline to avoid a blind double change.
alternatives: If coverage still plateaus with 8 layers, keep n_surface_layers=8 and instead raise max_thickness_to_medial_ratio and n_smooth_thickness (softer limiter, more smoothing) rather than cutting layers.

If the 90 deg TE creases keep disabling extrusion, raise n_buffer_cells_no_extrude to 1-2 (partial NOEXTRUDE spreading) or drop slip_feature_angle to 20 (extrude over slipping walls) - not done here to avoid two simultaneous crease changes.

If quality persists only at the TE box, add one local_refine level=5 box on X 0.90-1.05, |Y|<=0.10, Z <=0.15 (legal, one level above surface level 4, small area); rejected for now because cells share the 2M gate and the failure is extrusion, not resolution.

No restore is possible: none of plan:7932afe0cebdb8ce / f62967be11e235b5 / 2d715090c42f3a28 / 3dca9c5fca758495 is eligible_for_restore, and all four show the same 6 native failures, so the anchor hypothesis is untested.
counterevidence: All four prior rounds (round 0-3) share the identical 6 native failures and layer coverage 0.673-0.674, so no measured valid anchor exists; the layer mechanism has never been changed, only repair_* boxes added - those three boxes addressed the SAME sites and failed, so I add no more boxes.

feature_0 level-6 box overlaps the TE strip and imposes a level-4 to level-6 jump (two levels > n_cells_between_levels=3 buffer); it is a plausible contributor to the 1783 concave faces / 1470 concave cells, but removing it would coarsen a genuine sampled geometry feature without flow evidence, so I leave it and instead damp layer-driven distortion via the other settings.
n_grow is deliberately NOT increased: it propagates non-extrusion and would LOWER coverage below 0.90 rather than fill uncovered faces.
No flow probe and no actual y+, so no wall_height and no assertion of physical/RANS accuracy; this is a mesh-mechanism repair only.
Whole-body coverage is area-weighted; a local success at the TE box cannot by itself certify the 90% gate.

actions.why: Shift the layer driver from all-or-nothing non-extrusion to soft thickness limiting: the mover reduced thickness at 0 nodes because max_thickness_to_medial_ratio=0.3 was never reached against the real medial field, so columns beside non-extruded faces inverted. Trimming the installed stack to 6 layers (~0.0123 m) at unchanged first height keeps p50 y+ behaviour while fitting under the TE-strip p50 solid half-thickness of 0.00735 m and under the medial room; lowering layer feature_angle to 45 suppresses extrusion at the ~90 deg (p50=p95=90) TE/tip creases where 50.8-54.3% of edges already exceed 60; the medial-ratio and smoothing changes make the limiter act before inversion. n_grow stays 0 because it propagates NON-EXTRUSION and would reduce coverage.

Cleaner surface snapping reduces the normal misalignment that feeds the medial-axis mover's collision at the TE strip: the same box holds 222 meshQualityFaces, 192 wrong-oriented faces and 159 low-vol-ratio faces at median wall distance 0.0273 m with measured local feature 0.0507 m. More feature-snap iterations and stronger patch/tolerance smoothing before the layer pass is the causal counterpart to the layer change, not a second unrelated intervention.

advisor.hypothesis: The mesh is a first attempt with no native failure evidence; the one measured, deterministic defect is that the off-body requirements are effectively unrefined (configured coverage 0.00386 / 0.00182 / 0.00181). Cause: refinement is purely distance-driven around the body (bands 0.03125 m @ L4 and 0.09375 m @ L3) plus one level-6 near-trailing-edge feature box; nothing follows the flow downstream of X=0.996. The trailing-edge vorticity sheet and the two tip-vortex corridors are transport features, not proximity features, so they must be prescribed explicitly. Fixing this with three flow_refine boxes at level 3 (0.25/2^3 = 0.03125 m) satisfies both declared spans with margin (wake 0.03125 < 0.06226 m; tips 0.03125 < 0.04981 m), keeps the level jump to the level-4 surface mesh at exactly one level (n_cells_between_levels=3 inserts a buffer), and is consistent with the existing level-3 outer distance band so the union is a single level-3 block with no internal transition. Level 3 is the coarsest level that meets the strict max axis span; level 2 (0.0625 m) would exceed the tip span (0.0625 > 0.0498) and would only pass via the native p95 1.5x tolerance, and level 4 would cost ~680k extra cells and break the 2M gate. I deliberately do NOT touch layers, first height, n_grow or snap: there is no native extrusion/quality evidence yet, and the planning y+ estimate (h1 = 1.1087e-3 m, y+~50, stack 0.01829 m) is a surrogate, not a measurement.
advisor.expected_change: Scenario screen flips from accepted=false to accepted=true with configured volume coverage 0.00386/0.00182/0.00181 -> 1.0/1.0/1.0 for lift_wake/tip_left/tip_right, and nominal corridor cell size becomes 0.03125 m everywhere inside the corridors instead of 0.25 m background and 0.0625 m in the un-banded wake, downstream to X=2.9886 (3 chords past the trailing edge). Conservative cell forecast rises 1,693,778 -> 1,821,185 (91% of the 2,000,000 budget, +85k, i.e. less than the naive 8x-per-increment because the union of the three equal-level boxes is refined once). Uncertainty: the forecast is an unvalidated geometry upper bound and actual native cell count is a hard gate; the corridors themselves remain unvalidated hypotheses, so this intervention fixes resolution allocation, not vortex position or flow accuracy.
counterevidence: The corridors are unvalidated_physical_hypothesis: incidence/deflection may move the rolled-up tip vortex, so refining exactly the declared envelope could still miss the physical core - I keep the boxes matched to the requirement bounds instead of spending the remaining 9% budget on speculative enlargement.

Geometry measurements show p5 solid_normal_half_thickness 0.00845 m at thin TE/tip stations versus a requested layer stack of 0.01829 m and max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3, and 33.4% of adjacent edges exceed the 60 deg layer feature angle, so extrusion may still trim or drop layers at the TE/tip - that is a separate mechanism with no native evidence yet.

unresolved_feature_fraction stays 0.0366 with and without the new boxes, confirming that off-body refinement does not address the unresolved sub-grid cluster and must not be sold as a geometry-fidelity fix.
Steady RANS mesh allocation cannot validate wake recovery or any unsteady shedding implied by the vorticity-sheet mechanism.
alternatives: Refine the same three corridors at level 4 (0.015625 m): passes spans with large margin but adds ~680k cells (conservative total ~2.37M) and would exceed max_global_cells, so it is not admissible now.
Refine the wake at level 2 (0.0625 m) to save ~43k cells: rejected because 0.0625 m exceeds the declared tip max span 0.04981 m and only the native p95 1.5x tolerance would mask it for the wake.

Widen refinement_bands (e.g. inner 0.03125 m @ L4, outer 0.15 m @ L3) to give the medial-axis shrinker more room around the thin TE/tip: deferred - it is cheap but unevidenced, and the thin-station half-thickness above suggests the shrinker, not the band depth, is the controlling risk.
Enlarge/shift the corridors beyond their declared bounds to hedge vortex drift: deferred until a flow solution exists, since it consumes the remaining budget margin with no measured trajectory.
